furniture_v4.storyboard:
Furniture journey v4: storyboard, prompts and asset plan (single source of truth).

Storyline (user brief, 2026-09-27): chair in the lounge -> zoom into the oak -> the chair comes
apart -> one piece, the oak leg frame, is picked -> it travels back to the factory where these leg
frames are made -> zoom into the oak, the QR is laser-etched -> pull out onto the chair in the lounge,
a phone scans the QR -> the chair floats to the repair workshop.

The ten question stops stay (the assessment scores all ten); the story maps onto them:

 1 company   Lounge, wide: the chair by the tall windows (selector card, no question)
 2 product   The chair, closer, left of frame
 3 material  Oak grain macro: the outer face of the side rail of the chair's near leg frame
 4 component The chair taken apart: its real parts float in the lounge (exploded view)
 5 supplier  The oak leg frame (front leg, rear leg, armrest, side rail) floats forward, alone
 6 logistics The leg frame arrives in the component factory's dispatch hall (pallets of frames)
 7 factory   It lands on the bed of the laser engraver in the same hall
 8 data      Oak grain macro again: the same rail, the prduct.com QR freshly laser-etched
 9 passport  The chair in the lounge: a hand holds a phone to the QR on the side rail
10 nextLife  The chair has floated to the repair workshop bench

Principles:
- Same object, same pixels: the chair, its parts and the leg frame are cut out once and re-used in
  every still they appear in (the leg frame is planar, so a homography places it in any pose).
- Real motion: every move is a 2.5D layer animation (tools/rig.py) of those objects and plates -
  parts float apart, the frame glides, turns, travels, lands; the chair lifts and flies - which
  LTX-2.5 re-renders at denoise 0.975 into generated footage, guided by BOTH end stills.
- The same texture both ways: stops 3 and 8 are one hi-res oak macro; the push in and the pull out
  meet on exactly that image.
- Definition: stills and clips pass through SeedVR2 7B at 2560x1440.
